prompt: An investment of $\$400$ grows by $6\%$ each year. Which expression gives the value of the investment, in dollars, after $t$ years?
hint: Growth by a fixed percent each year is different from growth by a fixed dollar amount. Does it call for repeated adding or repeated multiplying?

hints.text: Growth by a fixed percent each year is different from growth by a fixed dollar amount. Does it call for repeated adding or repeated multiplying?
Each year the value keeps its full $100\%$ and gains $6\%$ more, so it is multiplied by $1.06$. Apply that multiplier $t$ times to $400$.
Multiplying by $1.06$ a total of $t$ times gives $400(1.06)^t$, which is choice B.

learningObjective: Build an exponential growth model from a percent rate.
explanation: A $6\%$ increase keeps the original $100\%$ and adds $6\%$ more, so each year the value is multiplied by $1.06$.
Repeating that multiplication for $t$ years gives the exponential expression $400(1.06)^t$.
Choice A adds only $6$ cents per year, choice C keeps only $6\%$ each year, and choice D multiplies the value by $6$ each year.
The correct model is $400(1.06)^t$, which is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check with one year
steps: After one year, $\$400$ growing $6\%$ should be $\$424$.
Test each choice at $t = 1$: A gives $400.06$, B gives $424$ ✓, C gives $24$, D gives $2400$.
A single well-chosen test value eliminates three choices instantly, and $t = 1$ is almost always the right one to pick.
